answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a anchor as the anchor of the cost.
